The 2002 sentence ends at 'any contained program'; 2023 appends 'unless they are defined as external files in each of the source elements in which they are referenced'. The base words are identical in both editions, and the 2023 exception only has content if those words reach the case it excepts: a contained program that describes the containing program's external file again (its own FD XF IS EXTERNAL, same file connector) and does I-O on it. Read in 2002's own text, that I-O references 'the file' of the containing program's non-GLOBAL FD (one external file connector), which SR3 forbids; the 2002 EXTERNAL GR2 b permission is a general rule and does not name SR3 as an exception. 2023 E.3.3 calls its addition a clarification, but that is the later edition's view and does not decide the 2002 rule. The reader's equivalence rests on reading 'the file' as the local file-name only, which the text does not settle. Probe (reader's): global_ext_file.cob, contained GEXTI writes to its own FD XF IS EXTERNAL, accepted and run at --std 2002 ('R1 OUT1 / R2 IN-2').
